messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Streaming tail latency SLO breach detected for route /v1/stream in region us-west2. p95=480ms (SLO=300ms), p99=1.8s (SLO=800ms). Error-rate stable. Auto-escalation -> severity: high. Paging oncall.

alice.nguyen: ack, I'm on it. Seeing alerts in the console (per-route) and the streaming exporter shows a spike starting ~1758882400.

oliver.sre: joining. any customer-facing services reported errors? @liz.support

liz.support: one customer reported intermittent stalls in chat streaming, timestamps match. No new error budget requests yet but they flagged slow turntimes.

maya.neteng: I see packet drops on the egress NAT gw path for the us-west2-azb -> azc interzone route during the window. Spike in retransmits and SYN handshake timeouts. Flow logs show a rise in retransmits ~1758882385.

ben.kumar: can you paste the telemetry percentiles from the streaming gateway? Also any recent deploys? @deploy-bot

deploy-bot: no active deploys in the last 90 minutes. Last canary completed at 1758881000.

alice.nguyen: telemetry from streaming-gw-prod-usw2:
```
window: 1758882360-1758882460
p50: 35ms
p95: 482ms
p99: 1802ms
streaming stalls (>5s): 0.8% -> baseline 0.02%
```

oliver.sre: thanks. maya can you share a sample tcpdump / netstat around the egress NAT? any SYN retransmit counts or conntrack saturation?

maya.neteng: quick outputs:
```
# conntrack -S | grep tcp
tcp      15342
# ip -s link show eth0
RX packets 1,234,567 errors 0 dropped 6 overruns 0 frame 0
TX packets 1,111,222 errors 0 dropped 0
# tcptrace (summary) -> retransmits jump from 0.1% -> 2.6% on nat-gw-3
```
Also saw DNS timeouts to internal resolver (10.10.0.5) ~30-60ms extra and some TLS handshake retransmits to downstream service ip 172.31.9.17.

ben.kumar: interesting — if DNS to internal resolver is slow, that could add tail to connection setup which affects short lived streaming substreams. Any correlation with ephemeral port exhaustion on nat-gw-3?

maya.neteng: ephemeral port usage peaked near conntrack limit on nat-gw-3. We hit a conntrack high-water which caused dropped new flows. Running "conntrack -L | wc -l" returned ~65530 (threshold 65536). Likely affecting new TLS handshakes.

alice.nguyen: that explains p99 tail. Mitigation options: 1) temporarily increase conntrack on nat-gw-3 and rollout config, 2) failover egress path to nat-gw-4 pool, 3) apply per-route aggressive connection reuse at streaming-gw. Thoughts?

oliver.sre: do 2 and 1: immediate traffic steer to nat-gw-4 then increase conntrack entries on nat-gw-3 to avoid reoccurrence. Maya can you trigger egress reroute? I can patch conntrack sysctl on the node pool if approved.

maya.neteng: initiating egress reroute now. Command:
```
# aws ec2 modify-network-interface-attribute --network-interface-id eni-0abc123 --attachment "{"InstanceId":"i-0f...","DeviceIndex":1}" 
# update route-table: set nat-gw target -> nat-gw-4
```

(2 minutes later)

maya.neteng: reroute applied, BGP convergence looks clean. Telemetry starting to show drop in retransmits.

alice.nguyen: increasing conntrack on nat-gw-3: running `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=131072` and persisting in config. Pushing now.

deploy-bot: sysctl change applied to 8 nodes in pool-egress-usw2.

(5 minutes later)

alice.nguyen: metrics update:
```
window: 1758882660-1758882860
p95: 110ms
p99: 240ms
streaming stalls (>5s): 0.03%
retransmit rate: 0.2%
```
Looks like reroute + conntrack increase mitigated the tail. Rolling monitor for 30m.

ben.kumar: customer impact note for postmortem: small subset of customers experienced streaming stalls and degraded tail latency for ~8 minutes. Impacted feature: streaming chat turns; no token loss. Liz can you notify affected customers with timeline and mitigation steps?

liz.support: will draft message: include explanation of transient egress NAT saturation and mitigations (reroute, conntrack increase), apologize, offer contact. Will send to ops-review for approval.

oliver.sre: next steps: 1) run root cause: why conntrack spiked — long lived ephemeral flows? any spike in webhook fanout? 2) add runbook entry: automatic failover if conntrack > 75% to nat-gw-4, 3) add alert for internal DNS latency > 50ms correlated with conntrack.

maya.neteng: I'll follow up on flow patterns; initial guess is increased short-lived TLS sessions due to a retry storm from a downstream proxy causing connection churn.

alice.nguyen: I'll open the incident postmortem and include command outputs, timeline, mitigations, and customer impact. Moving to monitoring mode; paging stopped.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: severity reduced to monitoring. Please add notes to incident tracker: ID INC-1758882468."
